feedback: Before this candidate races, the evidence supports the y = 0.07 m step. Iteration 0 to 1 showed that moving the sensors from y = 0.04 to y = 0.06 m raised oval finishes from 0 to 4 of 20 and slalom progress from 0.11 to 0.14 (iteration 0 and 1 outcome tables). Iteration 4 then reached slalom progress 0.278 with max_error 0.0638 m and only 1.05 line losses per run, so the remaining slalom failure looks like late reaction rather than lost sensing. Because the integrator's ki = 0.2 and kd = 0.6 were introduced in iteration 4, that controller is held unchanged here. Those terms are the part of the controller I had to add to work with this geometry. The integral term counters the fixed motor mismatch, and the higher kd reduced oval oscillation from 0.21 to 0.19. Whether the improvement came from ki or kd is not yet separated. I state no outcome for this candidate. What to change depends on the next race: if the oval or s-bend completion falls below the iteration-4 levels (20 of 20 and 18 of 20), y = 0.07 m is too far forward and should be reverted to 0.06 m. If the slalom still fails with max_error near 0.06 m and line losses at or below 2 per run, look-ahead is no longer the limit, so hold the geometry and I will tune the controller. Widening the spread is only justified if slalom line losses exceed about 2 per run with progress below 0.2.
requested_changes: Keep body, wheels, track, sensor size and mass (0.6 kg) as proposed, and test y = 0.07 m with x = ±0.024 m, so the look-ahead is the only geometry change.
If oval or s-bend completion drops below 20 of 20 and 18 of 20 respectively, revert the sensors to y = 0.06 m rather than changing the spread or the body.
If slalom line_loss_events exceed about 2 per run with slalom progress below 0.2, widen the spread to x = ±0.032 m at y = 0.07 m, keeping five sensors.
